0.long_answer: The hormone linked to nocturnal enuresis is antidiuretic hormone (ADH), which is also known as arginine vasopressin. Normally, ADH is released in a circadian rhythm, with higher amounts during the night to reduce urine production by prompting the kidneys to reabsorb water. When there is an insufficient release of this hormone at night, excessive urine is produced, which can lead to bedwetting. This is why treatments such as desmopressin, a synthetic form of ADH, are used to help manage this condition by mimicking the effects of natural ADH.
